newsitem.title: USA: Reno reviews requests for U.S. campaign probes.
newsitem.headline: Reno reviews requests for U.S. campaign probes.

text.p: The Justice Department is reviewing separate requests for an independent counsel to investigate alleged campaign finance violations, Attorney General Janet Reno said Thursday.
"I have not received a report from the criminal division yet. I would anticipate that soon," she said at the weekly Justice Department news briefing.

Sen. John McCain asked Oct. 11 for an independent probe on whether the Democratic Party has received illegal foreign contributions. The Arizona Republican cited news reports of nearly $1 million in contributions from individuals tied to Lippo Group, an Indonesian company.

McCain, a key supporter of Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, said he believed it would be impossible in an election-year for any Clinton administration officials to determine if there had been any violations of the law or ethical lapses.

The other request was made Oct. 9 by the citizens' lobbying group Common Cause alleging violations of finance laws by the Democratic and Republican presidential campaigns. The White House and Dole's campaign denied any wrongdoing.

Reno said she did not know if the Justice Department would act on the requests before the Nov. 5 elections. She has said in the past she has not tried to speed up or slow down a decision. "The best way to do it is to let the career people in the criminal division do it in an orderly way, consistent with the law and consistent with prior processes used in similar cases."
